title: Hajj origins and significance
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Sawm, Zakah and Khums, Hajj (3.3 to 3.5)
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y10 lesson 29 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Hajj origins and significance)
intro: Lesson 29: 3.5 Hajj: nature, role, origins and significance. To understand the nature, origins and significance of Hajj, from Ibrahim (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام) to the Prophet ﷺ

questions.q: Describe the origins of Hajj. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Ibrahim left Hajar and Ismail in Makkah; Hajar's search between Safa and Marwah and Zamzam; Ibrahim and Ismail built the Ka'bah (2:127); Ibrahim proclaimed Hajj (22:27).
questions.model: One mark per accurate point: 1) Hajar and Ismail in the valley; 2) Safa and Marwah and Zamzam (Bukhari, from Ibn Abbas); 3) the Ka'bah built (2:127); 4) the call to Hajj (22:27).

questions.q: Hajj is due on those who are ...
6-mark answer in the portal response box (our own question): 'Explain the significance of Hajj for Muslims.' Two developed points with evidence. Start: 'Hajj is significant because ...'
questions.a: Forgiveness (Bukhari and Muslim: return like the day born), equality and unity of the ummah, obedience to a pillar (3:97), following Ibrahim; developed
questions.model: Teacher writes point 1: 'Hajj is significant because it brings forgiveness. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever performs Hajj without obscenity or sin returns like the day his mother bore him (Bukhari and Muslim).'

questions.a: Here I am, O Allah, here I am; You have no partner; praise, blessing and dominion are Yours

questions.q: Back to our ponder: what does Hajj say about Islam?
questions.a: One God, one ummah, equality before Allah
